The claim contains three parts. 1. 'Requires careful choice of error norm': Supported. The text states, 'In principle, any error norm can be chosen... We note that the error norm has a high impact on the efficiency and quality of the clustering algorithm... We suggest the following norm'. 2. 'Performance depends on data distribution': Partially supported/Implicit. The text mentions 'Tile Lookup... For evenly distributed data, achieve this by regular decomposition', implying performance/methods depend on distribution, but it doesn't explicitly state general 'performance' (like accuracy or convergence speed) depends on it in the same direct way as the error norm. However, the lookup time optimization is tied to distribution. 3. 'PCA variants assume local manifold structure': Unsupported. The provided text discusses 'adaptive clustering', 'wavelet transforms', and 'topological structures of two-manifold surfaces'. It does not mention PCA (Principal Component Analysis) or PCA variants at all. Therefore, this part of the claim is not supported by the evidence.

If a tile contains more than $n_{max}$ points, $n_{max}$ points are selected randomly [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that if a tile contains more than $n_{max}$ points, $n_{max}$ points are selected randomly. This is explicitly confirmed in the provided text under the section '2.5 Conclusions Concerning Clustering', which lists modifications to reduce computational cost. One of the bullet points states: 'The number of points that determine an approximating function ˜f j k ... must be bounded by a constant nmax. If a tile contains more than nmax points, we select nmax of them randomly.' Additionally, the notes section reiterates this: 'nmax: Maximum number of points determining an approximating function f̃^j_k. If a tile contains more than nmax points, select nmax points randomly.'

4.  **Refinement:** Refine all tiles $\tau_k^j$ corresponding to residuals $\varepsilon_k^j$ greater than a specified threshold, rather than refining one by one, allowing exponential growth of clusters with level index $j$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence supports refining all tiles corresponding to residuals greater than a threshold to allow exponential growth of clusters. Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Conclusions Concerning Clustering' section: 'This can be achieved by refining all tiles τ^j_k corresponding to residuals ε^j_k greater than a specified threshold.' It also notes that 'the number of clusters grows exponentially with the level index j' when more than one cluster is refined in this manner. The notes section also reiterates this exact strategy. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

Modifications such as threshold-based refinement and point bounding reduce the cost to expected linear time for large-scale datasets [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'Conclusions Concerning Clustering' section that modifications are necessary to make the algorithms applicable to large-scale data sets, and lists these modifications as: 1) refining all tiles with residuals greater than a specified threshold (threshold-based refinement), 2) bounding the number of points determining an approximating function by a constant nmax (point bounding), and 3) estimating residuals based on a different set of points. The text directly asserts that these modifications reduce the computational cost to expected linear time.
